answer: Each agent allocates fixed 64 GB glacier buffer in physical RAM. On epoch pulse, verifier broadcasts cryptographic seed. Agent runs pointer-chase through RAM: pseudo-random offsets scatter like sparse nebula across cache lines, folding each fetched word into rolling Blake3 digest. Verifier checks final cryptographic seal against latency bound under 18 milliseconds. Emulation on cheap swap fails timing checks; faking thousand nodes demands 64 TB unshared DDR5 memory costing 14000 dollars monthly. Missed window triggers immediate identity burn.
